draft.title: Choosing and reading graphs
card: Column and bar
These graphs use bars to compare amounts in separate categories, such as rainfall in different cities. Column graph bars stand upright. Bar graph bars lie sideways.
Line
A line graph joins points in order along the horizontal axis. It suits data that changes over time, such as a town's rainfall each month.
Picture
A picture graph uses small symbols to stand for a number of items. A legend beside it shows what one symbol means.
Reading
To read any graph, check the title, the axis labels, the units and the scale before you look at the shapes.

2.alt: A line graph of monthly rainfall in a town. Rainfall rises from 20 mm in January to 80 mm in March, then falls to 40 mm in May.

draft.remember: Compare categories with columns or bars. Show change over time with a line.

a.q: Which graph best shows how a river's height changed each day for a month?
opts: A line graph
A picture graph
A bar graph of one day
A column graph of the cities
a.why: A line graph joins points in order, so it shows change over time. A column graph compares separate categories, so it is tempting, but daily river heights are a series in order, not separate groups.
a.clue: Which graph is best at showing change over time?

b.q: Priya has the number of students who travel to school by bus, car, bike or foot. Which graph suits this data best?
opts: A column graph with one column for each way
A line graph joining bus, car, bike and foot
A line graph of travel over twelve months
A picture graph with no symbol meaning given
b.why: Bus, car, bike and foot are separate categories, so a column graph compares them well. A line graph joins points as if they were in order, which they are not here.
b.clue: Are the ways of travelling in any order, or are they separate groups?

b.best: A column graph with one column for each way
